Hi Rachel,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — we like Redwood's runtime and the private/VPC options. Before we proceed to signature we need to validate a few deployment/control items so our security and procurement teams can clear the order form/MSA redlines. Attached is our current SOW for context (Solstice_SOW_v3.pdf).

High level asks from legal/security:
- Confirm whether Redwood will allow an operator to perform limited maintenance on our on-premises instance and, if so, list exact allowed activities.
- Proof-of-control evidence: sample operator runbook, a brief operator attestation template, and a description of how snapshots/snapshots transfers would be handled (who signs, transfer logs).
- Key custody model: confirm support for customer-managed keys (BYOK) vs Redwood-managed KMS; if Redwood manages keys, what attestations are available?
- Audit windows / witness: we may request an audit window (remote observation) for a one-time snapshot transfer if needed. Need to understand typical duration and process.

Can you route this to the right contacts on your side (legal/contracts + technical leads)? We can also share a redline but wanted to gather evidence items first.

Attachment: Solstice_SOW_v3.pdf (proposal & installation appendix)

Thanks,

Jordan — thanks for the clear checklist and the SOW. Looping in David (Head of Contracts) and Marissa (Legal Ops) to propose a practical path forward. Quick plan from our side:

1) We will produce a short evidence pack (operator runbook excerpt, operator attestation template, and snapshot transfer checklist) by EOD Friday.
2) On the MSA/order form we typically accept a narrow set of operator activities (install, upgrades, emergency patching) documented in an Exhibit. We can draft an Exhibit tailoring permitted activities and escalation contacts.
3) For key custody: we support BYOK for encryption at rest. For customers that choose Redwood-managed KMS we can provide signed attestation and KMS audit logs on request — I will confirm exact log retention with infra.
4) Audit/witness approach: propose "witness-lite" remote observation for snapshot transfers (2–4 hour window) unless Solstice needs onsite witnessing. Details to be agreed in Order Form Exhibit.

Jordan / Rachel — thanks for the context. I reviewed the SOW and drafted a compact approach that should address Solstice's controls appetite while keeping the MSA/order form actionable. High level proposal (summary):

- Operator scope: carve out a short Exhibit A (Operator Activities) enumerating allowed tasks (listed examples: install, version upgrades, emergency security patching, limited telemetry collection for support). Any activity outside Exhibit A requires customer written approval.
- Auditable proof: require operator actions be logged and exported; agreed format is a signed JSON manifest plus transfer logs retained for 90 days.
- Snapshot transfer and witness: allow snapshot transfer to an escrow-styled custodian for contingency scenarios. We propose a "witness-lite" flow — Redwood performs transfer to an escrow agent (TerraFirma Escrow) and provides a signed transfer manifest; customer may request a remote audit session during transfer (standard window proposed: up to 4 hours).
- Key custody compromise: accept BYOK as default for customers who need exclusive control. For Redwood-managed KMS we will include a Vendor Attestation Annex describing HSM usage and ability to produce KMS audit logs on request.

Suggested contract artifacts attached (redline_msa_solstice_20280520.docx) — this is a starting point, not final. Specific snippets included in the doc: sample Exhibit A language, transfer manifest example, and a short escrow-lite clause to insert into the Order Form.

If Solstice wants a stricter in-person witnessing model we can negotiate exhibit fees and scheduling.

— David
David Kim

David — appreciate the pragmatic approach and the redline. A few clarifying questions before we circulate internally:

1) For the snapshot transfer manifest — can Redwood commit to including a signed hash of the snapshot (SHA256) plus a UTC timestamp and operator identifier? That will satisfy our integrity checks.
2) For KMS: BYOK is our preference. If we elect Redwood-managed KMS, will Redwood permit export of KMS audit logs to our SIEM for the transfer event? What format and retention?
3) Audit window: 4 hours sounds reasonable. Our security team would like a 2-business-day scheduling lead time and the ability to escalate to a 1-day onsite witness if remote observation uncovers concerns.

We will do a quick internal review; can you confirm an estimated date for final DocuSign-ready MSA + Order Form? Also we have a short list of follow-up questions — attaching as questions_list.txt.

Thanks,
Jordan
